title: Mrs. Michal Tawil: Set Me Free (Class # 28)

chapters.title: Introduction to Rosh Hashanah and Freedom
chapters.about: Preparation for Rosh Hashanah, the avodah of the holiday, and the connection between freedom and the shofar.

chapters.title: Personal Reflections on Hosting and Limitations
chapters.about: A personal story about hosting grandchildren, recognizing personal limitations, and accepting reality.

chapters.title: The Mitzvah of the Shofar
chapters.about: Discussion on Rabbi Moshe Shapira's teaching that listening to the shofar is the primary obligation of Rosh Hashanah.

chapters.title: Freedom from the Expectations of Others
chapters.about: Overcoming the enslavement of trying to please people and how the shofar calls us to true freedom.

chapters.title: Compassion, the Womb, and Parasha Ekev
chapters.about: The meaning of rachamim as a womb, letting Hashem do the work, and finding importance in small details connected to Parasha Ekev.

claims: "She explores how trusting Hashem and relinquishing the need to please others or control everything allows one to step out of emotional enslavement." - The teacher does not use the specific phrase 'emotional enslavement'.
"Through personal reflections and examples, she teaches how to embrace personal truth and make space for growth." - The teacher does not use the phrase 'embrace personal truth'.
summary: Mrs. Tawil discusses preparing for Rosh Hashanah by examining the spiritual work of freedom, letting go of expectations, and listening to the shofar. She explores how trusting Hashem and relinquishing the need to please others or control everything allows one to step out of emotional enslavement. Through personal reflections and examples, she teaches how to embrace personal truth and make space for growth.
questions: What is the main obligation on Rosh Hashanah according to the class?
How is the blowing of the shofar connected to the concept of freedom?
What does it mean to relinquish expectations and let Hashem into our daily challenges?
How can paying attention to small details, such as laundry, shift our perspective on life and responsibilities?
